location.en: Lantern Park, the campfire circle by the lake

goal.en: Welcome a nervous newcomer and share what you learned this year.
goal.zh: 歡迎緊張的新成員，分享你這一年學到的經驗。

background: lakeside park clearing at early evening, a crackling campfire in a stone ring, wooden log benches around it, string lights between maple trees, calm lake beyond

intro.en: Evening at Lantern Park. The Campfire Chat circle is bigger than ever tonight.
intro.zh: 傍晚的燈籠公園。今晚的營火英語社，人比以往都多。

intro.en: A young woman sits alone at the edge of the circle, holding a notebook like a shield. She looks exactly like you did a year ago.
intro.zh: 一個年輕女生獨自坐在圈子邊緣，把筆記本抱在胸前像盾牌一樣。她看起來，就跟一年前的你一模一樣。

intro.en: Hi... um, is this the English conversation group? I just arrived in Maple Bay last week.
intro.zh: 嗨……呃，這裡是英語會話社嗎？我上週才剛到楓灣。

lines.en: I'm Hana. Everyone here sounds so fluent. I'm a little scared to say anything.
lines.zh: 我叫花奈。這裡每個人講話都好流利，我有點不敢開口。

choices.en: I know the feeling. I was terrified at my first campfire too.
choices.zh: 我懂那種感覺。我第一次來營火社也超緊張。
choices.tip: 先用 I know the feeling. 表達同理，比急著給建議更能讓對方放鬆。

choices.en: Then don't be scared. Just talk. It's really not that hard.
choices.zh: 那就不要怕啊，開口講就好，真的沒那麼難。

lines.en: Oh. Okay. Easy for you to say, I guess.

story.en: Hana nods politely and goes quiet for the rest of the night. Your "encouragement" works more like a cold shower.
story.zh: 花奈禮貌地點點頭，整晚再也沒說話。你的「鼓勵」效果比較像一桶冷水。

fail.why: 對緊張的人說「不要怕、沒那麼難」，聽起來像在否定對方的感受。先同理再鼓勵：I know the feeling. I was nervous too.

choices.en: Don't worry. Slowly slowly you will get used to it, I promise.
choices.zh: 別擔心，慢慢你就會習慣了，我保證。

lines.en: Slowly... slowly? Sorry, is that an expression here?
lines.zh: 慢慢……慢慢？抱歉，這是這邊的說法嗎？

story.en: Hana carefully writes "slowly slowly" in her notebook as a new local phrase. You decide not to tell her the truth tonight.
story.zh: 花奈認真地把 slowly slowly 抄進筆記本，當成當地新說法。你決定今晚先不告訴她真相。

fail.why: 「慢慢」直譯成 slowly slowly 不是自然英文。可以說 You'll get used to it in time. 或 It gets easier, little by little.。

lines.en: Really? So... do you have any advice? What should I do first?
lines.zh: 真的嗎？那……你有什麼建議嗎？我應該先做什麼？

choices.en: If I were you, I'd come here every week. Regulars become friends.
choices.zh: 如果我是你，我會每週都來。常來的人都會變成朋友。
choices.tip: If I were you, I'd... 是給建議最自然的句型，語氣溫和不命令。

choices.en: If I am you, I will come here every single week. It helps a lot.
choices.zh: 如果我是你，我會每個禮拜都來，很有幫助。

lines.en: If you are me? But... you're you. I'm confused.
lines.zh: 如果你是我？可是……你就是你啊。我搞糊塗了。

story.en: You spend ten minutes explaining that you are not, in fact, Hana. The advice gets lost somewhere along the way.
story.zh: 你花了十分鐘解釋自己真的不是花奈。建議本身，在過程中不見了。

fail.why: 「如果我是你」是與事實相反的假設，要用假設語氣：If I were you, I'd...。If I am you 文法上不成立。

choices.en: Honestly, my first week here was a mess. I lost my umbrella twice!
choices.zh: 老實說，我來的第一週一團亂，雨傘還弄丟兩次！

lines.en: Oh no. So... should I buy a strong umbrella first?
lines.zh: 喔不。所以……我應該先買把耐用的雨傘？

story.en: Hana's first piece of advice in Maple Bay is about umbrellas. She buys three the next day, just in case.
story.zh: 花奈在楓灣得到的第一個建議跟雨傘有關。隔天她一口氣買了三把，以防萬一。

fail.why: 對方問「我該先做什麼」，要給具體建議，不是只分享自己的糗事。分享經驗後要帶出重點：If I were you, I'd...。

lines.en: Every week. Got it. What about making friends outside class? People seem so busy.
lines.zh: 每週來，記下了。那課堂外要怎麼交朋友？大家看起來都好忙。

choices.en: It helps to say yes to invitations, even small ones like coffee.
choices.zh: 有人約就答應，很有幫助，就算只是喝杯咖啡也好。
choices.tip: It helps to + 原形動詞，用來分享「這樣做有幫助」的經驗，不會像在下指令。

choices.en: Ask them their age and salary first. Then you know where you stand.
choices.zh: 先問他們幾歲、薪水多少，這樣就知道彼此的關係了。

lines.en: Wouldn't that be... kind of rude here?
lines.zh: 在這裡這樣問……不會有點沒禮貌嗎？

story.en: Hana tries your tip at a party. Three people suddenly need to refill their drinks at the same time.
story.zh: 花奈在派對上試了你的建議。三個人突然同時想起要去加飲料。

fail.why: 在楓灣這類英語文化中，年齡和薪水屬於私人話題，剛認識就問會讓人尷尬。破冰可以聊興趣：What do you do for fun?

choices.en: It helps to saying yes to invitations, even small ones like lunch.
choices.zh: 有人約就答應會很有幫助，就算只是吃個午餐。

lines.en: It helps to saying? Is that... right? My teacher said something different.
lines.zh: It helps to saying？這樣對嗎？我老師講的好像不一樣。

story.en: Hana pulls out her grammar book, and you lose. Badly. In front of the whole circle.
story.zh: 花奈拿出文法書，你輸了，輸得很慘，還是在整個營火圈面前。

fail.why: It helps to 的 to 是不定詞，後面接原形動詞：It helps to say yes.。不能接 V-ing。

lines.en: That's really good advice. Honestly, I miss home already. Is that normal?
lines.zh: 這建議真的很好。老實說，我已經開始想家了。這樣正常嗎？

choices.en: Totally normal. What helped me was a weekly video call home.
choices.zh: 完全正常。對我有幫助的是每週跟家裡視訊一次。
choices.tip: What helped me was... 用自己的經驗給建議，比「你應該」更溫暖。

choices.en: You're an adult now, though. You really shouldn't feel homesick.
choices.zh: 可是你已經是大人了，真的不該想家啦。

lines.en: Oh. Right. Sorry for being childish, I guess.

story.en: Hana hides her homesickness from everyone for the next month. You were trying to help. It did not help.
story.zh: 接下來一個月，花奈把想家的心情藏得緊緊的。你本來想幫忙，結果幫倒忙。

fail.why: 說「你不應該有這種感覺」是在否定對方的情緒。先肯定再分享：Totally normal. What helped me was...。

choices.en: Very normal. Everyone will think home, especially late at night.
choices.zh: 很正常，每個人都會想家，尤其是晚上。

lines.en: Think home? Do you mean... think about home?

story.en: Hana corrects your English on her first week in Maple Bay. You both laugh, but you feel your teacher's eyes on you from across town.
story.zh: 花奈來楓灣第一週就糾正了你的英文。你們都笑了，但你彷彿感覺到遠方老師的視線。

fail.why: 「想家」不是 think home，要說 miss home 或 be homesick：It's normal to feel homesick.。

lines.en: Thank you so much, Kai. I feel a lot better. Can I sit next to you next week too?
lines.zh: 真的很謝謝你，凱。我好多了。下週我也可以坐你旁邊嗎？

choices.en: Of course. Save me a seat, and I'll introduce you around.
choices.zh: 當然。幫我留個位子，我帶你認識大家。
choices.tip: introduce you around 是「帶你認識大家」，對新人來說是最實際的歡迎。

choices.en: Of course! I'll introduce you to everyone who come every week.
choices.zh: 當然！我會介紹每週來的人給你認識。

lines.en: Everyone who come? I thought it was "everyone who comes." Sorry!
lines.zh: Everyone who come？我以為是 everyone who comes，抱歉！

story.en: Hana catches your mistake in five seconds. Clearly, she's going to be just fine here.
story.zh: 花奈五秒內就抓到你的錯。看來她在這裡一定會過得很好。

fail.why: everyone 視為單數，關係子句的動詞要加 s：everyone who comes。也可以簡單說 I'll introduce you around.。

choices.en: I guess so. Just don't follow me around all night, okay?
choices.zh: 應該可以吧。只是別整晚跟著我喔。

lines.en: Oh! No, of course not. I'll... sit somewhere else.
lines.zh: 喔！不會，當然不會。我……坐別的地方好了。

story.en: Hana sits on the far side of the fire next week. You remember how much one kind word meant to you a year ago.
story.zh: 下週花奈坐到營火的另一頭。你想起一年前，一句溫暖的話對你有多重要。

fail.why: 對方鼓起勇氣提出請求，冷淡回應會讓人退縮。熱情答應並提供幫助：Of course. Save me a seat.。

lines.en: Deal! I'll save you the best seat by the fire.
lines.zh: 說定了！我會幫你留營火旁最好的位子。

lines.en: Hana writes "If I were you, I'd..." in her notebook. You realize you have become the person you needed a year ago.
lines.zh: 花奈在筆記本寫下 If I were you, I'd...。你忽然發現，自己成了一年前最需要的那個人。

story.en: A year ago, someone made room for you by this fire. Tonight, you did the same for Hana.
story.zh: 一年前，有人在這堆營火旁為你挪出位子。今晚，你為花奈做了同樣的事。

notes.explain: 與事實相反的假設要用 were（不分人稱），後面接 I'd + 原形動詞。這是英文給建議最常見、最溫和的句型。

example.en: If I were you, I'd take the bus. It's faster.
example.zh: 如果我是你，我會搭公車，比較快。

notes.explain: 分享經驗時用 It helps to + 原形動詞，語氣像過來人的提醒，不像命令。也可以說 What helped me was...。

example.en: It helps to carry a small notebook for new words.
example.zh: 隨身帶一本小筆記本記新單字很有幫助。

notes.explain: 對方說出擔心或不安時，先用這句表達同理，再給建議，對方會更願意聽。

example.en: Your first week is overwhelming? I know the feeling.
example.zh: 第一週壓力很大？我懂那種感覺。

notes.explain: 「想家」不能直譯成 think home。要說 I miss home. 或 I feel homesick.。同理，「想你」是 I miss you.，不是 I think you.。

example.en: I felt homesick for the first two months.
example.zh: 前兩個月我一直很想家。

notes.en: What do you do for fun?
notes.explain: 在英語文化中，年齡、薪水、感情狀態都屬於私人話題，剛認識時不要問。聊興趣、週末計畫比較安全。

example.en: So, what do you do for fun on weekends?
example.zh: 那你週末都喜歡做什麼？
